landing.missionText: I never had the head space for a traditional volunteer role - work hours and fixed commitments just didn't line up. Still, I wanted to give something back. That idea became Afunto (Low German for "now and then"): volunteering without long-term commitment. Free and open for anyone to see. Built for the Oldenburg region. Usable by everyone.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.metaDescription: What personal data Afunto collects, why, how long it is kept, and the rights you have under the GDPR.
privacyPolicy.operatorNotConfigured: This deployment's operator hasn't configured a responsible party for data protection yet.
privacyPolicy.section2Title: Collection and storage of personal data
privacyPolicy.section2Body1: When visiting this website, general technical information is automatically processed (e.g. IP address, browser type, time of access) to ensure secure and reliable operation. This data can constitute personal data - including your IP address, per the Court of Justice of the EU's Breyer ruling (C-582/14) - even though we do not otherwise link it to your identity.
privacyPolicy.section2Body2: When registering and logging in via our authentication service (Keycloak), the data you enter (e.g. name, email address) is stored to enable you to use the platform.
privacyPolicy.section2Body3: You may also voluntarily add further details to your profile, such as a phone number organizations can reach you on, a profile picture, a short bio, and your skills and languages. Who this information is shared with or visible to is described in the following sections.
privacyPolicy.section2Body4: The legal basis for the technical access information described above is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in secure and reliable operation; your IP address is used only transiently, in memory, to enforce request rate limits, and is never stored. The legal basis for your registration and account data, including any optional profile fields you choose to add, is performance of the usage agreement with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). We retain your account and profile data for as long as your account exists; deleting your account, which you can do at any time from your profile settings, erases or anonymizes this data immediately. If we remove your account for violating our Terms of Use, your account and profile data is retained instead as moderation history, without an automatic deletion period. Notifications are deleted automatically 90 days after being read, or after 180 days if never read. Reports you file against content or other users (see "Reporting abusive content" on our Contact page) are retained as moderation history for as long as the reported account exists, and for up to 180 days afterwards; a report you filed yourself is deleted immediately together with the rest of your account data if you delete your own account. Audit logs of security-relevant actions (see below) are retained without an automatic deletion period.
privacyPolicy.section3Body: Personal data is only shared with third parties or made publicly accessible in the cases described in this section and its subsections below: when you sign up for an opportunity, as part of your public profile, and through the embedded third-party services for map display and location search. Any transfer beyond that only takes place if you have expressly consented or we are legally required to do so.
privacyPolicy.section3aBody: Opportunities on this platform are published by independent organizations. As described in our <termsLink>Terms of Use</termsLink>, these organizations are independent third parties and not part of our company; we are not a party to any agreement between you and the organization. When you sign up for an opportunity, we pass your name and email address, your phone number if you have added one to your profile, and any message you attach to your sign-up, to the publishing organization so it can reach you to coordinate the opportunity. The organization processes this data as an independent controller under Art. 4(7) GDPR in its own right and not as our processor; we have no influence over how the organization subsequently uses the data. The legal basis for this transfer is performance of the usage agreement with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR), which signing up for an opportunity fulfills.
privacyPolicy.section3bBody: Your profile - display name, profile picture, bio, listed skills and languages, earned badges, and your number of confirmed opportunities - is visible on a public profile page, without login, to anyone on the internet. Your email address and phone number are never shown on this page. The legal basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in making visible to organizations and other users who is active as a volunteer.
privacyPolicy.section3cTitle: Map display and location search (OpenStreetMap, Nominatim)
privacyPolicy.section3cBody: To display maps, your browser requests map tiles from our own backend, which in turn fetches them from the map-tile service provided by OpenStreetMap; the city search in the opportunity list filter is proxied the same way, through our backend, which queries the public Nominatim geocoding service (also operated by the OpenStreetMap Foundation). In both cases, only our backend server's IP address is transmitted to the OpenStreetMap Foundation - your own IP address and the search terms you type are never sent to it directly. The legal basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in providing functioning map and location-search features without disclosing your IP address to a third party. This is not data processing under Art. 28 GDPR; the OpenStreetMap Foundation only ever receives requests from our own infrastructure, not from you.
privacyPolicy.section4Body: When you upload a profile picture, or your organization adds a logo or an opportunity banner image, the file is stored on our self-hosted, S3-compatible object storage (RustFS). From the moment it is uploaded, the file is accessible via a public URL with no access restriction and no login required. A backup copy is additionally stored off-host, see the "Hosting and backups" section.
privacyPolicy.section5Body: We send emails that are necessary to operate your account and use the platform: to confirm your email address and to reset your password (via our authentication service, Keycloak), and notifications about sign-ups, confirmations, cancellations, reminders, and invitations. These are sent through an SMTP delivery provider with whom a data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR is in place. The legal basis is performance of the usage agreement with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Notifications that are not required to operate your account can be unsubscribed from in your profile settings or via the unsubscribe link in the respective email.
privacyPolicy.section6Body: This platform - including its database and object storage - runs on a server operated by Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany. The database and object storage are additionally backed up locally every day; these backups are further mirrored to a separate Hetzner Online GmbH object storage bucket so the platform can be restored if the server fails or is lost. Hetzner processes this data as our processor under Art. 28 GDPR; a corresponding data processing agreement (DPA) is in place with Hetzner. The legal basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in operating the platform reliably and being able to recover from data loss.
privacyPolicy.section7Body: Certain administrative actions - such as granting or revoking administrator rights, disabling or re-enabling an account, removing or restoring content, and administratively cancelling a sign-up - are logged with the acting user's ID, the type of action, the affected item, an optional reason, and the timestamp. This log is only accessible to platform administrators and serves to make administrative actions traceable and to protect against abuse. The legal basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in the security and integrity of the platform.
privacyPolicy.section7Body2: Our authentication service (Keycloak) separately logs authentication events - sign-ins, failed sign-in attempts, sign-outs, password changes, and account deletions - together with the IP address used and the timestamp, as well as administrative actions taken directly in its own admin console (such as password resets or role changes). This log lets us establish who accessed an account, from where, and when, which we need to assess and report the scope of a personal-data breach under Art. 33 GDPR. It is kept for 180 days and deleted automatically afterwards. The legal basis is our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) in the security of the platform and in meeting our breach-notification obligations.
privacyPolicy.section8Body1: This website uses one technically necessary cookie for authentication (a session cookie, set by our authentication service, Keycloak), and one further cookie, active-org, which remembers the organization you last opened so you return to the right dashboard; it is not used for authentication and is stored for up to one year. No tracking or advertising cookies are used.
privacyPolicy.section8Body2: We also store a small number of values in your browser's local storage: your selected interface language, whether you explicitly chose that language yourself rather than it being detected automatically, and which achievement notifications you have already seen (stored per account). Your session's access, ID, and refresh tokens are held separately in your browser's session storage, which is strictly necessary to keep you signed in and is cleared automatically when you close the browser tab. These values never leave your browser. The active-org cookie and these local storage and session storage values are cleared when you sign out.
privacyPolicy.section9Body1: You have the right to access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16 GDPR), erasure (Art. 17 GDPR), and restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR) of your personal data, as well as the right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR) and the right to object to processing carried out on the basis of our legitimate interest (Art. 21 GDPR). You can delete your own account and most associated data at any time from your profile settings; for any other request, including a copy of your data or an objection, contact us using the address or email given in the "Responsible party" section above. We aim to respond within one month, as required by Art. 12(3) GDPR.
privacyPolicy.section9Body2: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR), in particular in the German state where you live, work, or where an alleged infringement occurred. The authority responsible for us is: Die Landesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz Niedersachsen, Prinzenstraße 5, 30159 Hannover, Germany.

help.title: Help
help.intro: Answers to common questions for volunteers and organizations using Afunto. Can't find what you're looking for? See "Still need help?" below.
help.volunteersQ1: How do I sign up for a volunteer opportunity?
help.volunteersA1: Browse opportunities on the home page and open the one you're interested in. Opportunities with fixed time slots have a "Sign up for a slot" button - pick your slot and confirm with "Confirm sign-up". All others have an "Express interest" button where you send a short message.
help.volunteersQ2: How do I check in when I arrive?
help.volunteersA2: Opportunities that require check-in show a "Check in" button once your time slot starts. The organization may also check you in on-site using a QR code or your name.
help.volunteersQ3: Where can I see my sign-ups?
help.volunteersA3: Open your profile and go to the "My sign-ups" tab to see every past and upcoming sign-up.
help.organizersQ1: How do I get started as an organization?
help.organizersA1: Create an organization from the home page, then publish your first volunteer opportunity from your organization's dashboard.
help.organizersQ2: How do I publish a volunteer opportunity?
help.organizersA2: From your organization's dashboard, go to "Opportunities" and click "Create opportunity". Fill in the details and time slots, then publish it so volunteers can sign up.
help.organizersQ3: How do I manage volunteer sign-ups?
help.organizersA3: Open an opportunity from your organization's dashboard to see everyone who signed up, message them, or check them in.
help.organizersQ4: What is the difference between a member and an organizer?
help.organizersA4: Members see the organization's internal pages and its opportunities. Organizers can do everything members can, plus publish and manage opportunities, check volunteers in, invite people, change roles, and edit the organization's profile. Every organization keeps at least one organizer, so the last one cannot be demoted or leave.
help.organizersQ5: How do invitations to my organization work?
help.organizersA5: Invite people from the "Members" tab of your organization's dashboard and pick the role they should get. They receive an email and an in-app notification, and the invitation stays listed as pending until they accept or decline. Unanswered invitations expire after 14 days - the pending row shows the exact date, and you can resend an invitation at any time to start a fresh window or revoke it.
help.generalA1: No. Afunto is completely free and open source - for volunteers and organizations.
help.generalQ2: Do I need an account to take part?
help.generalA2: Not to browse - you can search every opportunity without signing up. To join one, you'll need a free account.
help.generalQ3: How fast can my organization get started?
help.generalA3: Register your organization in minutes and publish your first opportunity right away.
help.generalQ4: Is the code really open to inspect?
help.generalA4: Yes, the entire source code is available on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 license.
help.contactBody: If something looks like spam, fraud, or otherwise illegal content, use the "Report" button on the relevant <opportunitiesLink>opportunity</opportunitiesLink> or <organizationsLink>organization</organizationsLink> page. For anything else, visit our <contactLink>Contact page</contactLink>.

termsOfUse.title: Terms of Use
termsOfUse.metaDescription: The rules for using Afunto: our role as a platform, acceptable use, obligations for organizations, and liability.
termsOfUse.section1Body: These Terms of Use govern your use of Afunto (the "Platform"). By creating an account, registering for a volunteer opportunity, or otherwise using the Platform, you agree to be bound by these Terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the Platform.
termsOfUse.section2Body: Afunto is an intermediary that connects volunteers with opportunities published by independent organizations. We do not organize, supervise, or take part in the opportunities listed on the Platform, and we are not a party to any arrangement made between a volunteer and an organization. Organizations are solely responsible for the opportunities they publish, including their content, safety, and suitability.
termsOfUse.section3Body: When using the Platform, you agree to provide accurate information about yourself and keep it up to date, to treat other users, organizations, and the people you assist with respect, to follow the on-site instructions of the organization hosting an opportunity, and to refrain from posting or sharing content that is illegal, fraudulent, harassing, or otherwise harmful. You may not use the Platform to solicit paid work, collect personal data for unrelated purposes, or misrepresent your identity or affiliation with an organization.
termsOfUse.section4Body: Organizations that publish volunteer opportunities are responsible for the accuracy of their opportunities and for providing a safe environment at the location and time stated. If you come across content that looks like spam, fraud, or otherwise illegal, please use the report function described on our <contactLink>Contact page</contactLink>.
termsOfUse.section5Body: The Platform is provided on a best-effort, non-commercial basis. We do not guarantee the availability, accuracy, or completeness of any opportunity, and we are not liable for the conduct of volunteers or organizations, or for any loss, injury, or damage arising from participation in a volunteer opportunity. You take part in volunteer opportunities at your own risk. Nothing in this section limits liability that cannot be excluded under applicable law.
termsOfUse.section6Body: We may suspend or disable an account that violates these Terms, publishes fraudulent or unsafe content, or is the subject of substantiated reports from other users. Wherever possible, we will inform the affected account of the reason. You may stop using the Platform and request deletion of your account at any time; see our <privacyLink>Privacy Policy</privacyLink> for details on how your data is handled.
termsOfUse.section7Body: We may update these Terms from time to time to reflect changes to the Platform or legal requirements. Continued use of the Platform after an update constitutes acceptance of the revised Terms. For questions about these Terms, please contact us via the details listed in our <imprintLink>Imprint</imprintLink>.
